subsystems.name: Agent runtimes
subsystems.role: the isolation layer where each localized AI agent actually executes work.

subsystems.name: Task graph
subsystems.role: breaks incoming work into discrete, assignable tasks with dependencies.
parts: task schema (inputs, cost estimate, required capability)

subsystems.name: Priority governor
subsystems.role: the central policy engine that decides which agent gets which task right now.
parts: weighting rules per objective (speed, cost, accuracy)

subsystems.name: Telemetry and scoring
subsystems.role: measures real-time efficiency so the governor has something to optimise.
parts: quality or confidence scoring of outputs

subsystems.name: Learning loop
subsystems.role: adjusts priorities and routing as conditions change.

buildSteps.title: Define a task contract
buildSteps.detail: Specify a machine-readable description of every unit of work: required capability, expected duration, cost ceiling and acceptable output format. Without this, nothing downstream can be compared or routed.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the agents
buildSteps.detail: Wrap each agent so it emits standard traces and metrics (latency in milliseconds, tokens or compute consumed, success or failure) to one collection point.

buildSteps.title: Build the queue and graph
buildSteps.detail: Stand up a durable queue plus a dependency graph so tasks that must follow others are held back until their inputs exist.

buildSteps.title: Run a static scheduler first
buildSteps.detail: Assign tasks with fixed rules — capability match, round-robin, simple priority — to establish a baseline and expose bottleneck agents.

buildSteps.title: Add admission control
buildSteps.detail: Reject or delay work that would exceed a budget or overload a runtime, so the system fails gracefully instead of thrashing.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Feed measured latency, cost and quality back into the weighting rules, initially as hand-tuned thresholds rather than learned ones.

buildSteps.title: Simulate and replay
buildSteps.detail: Before changing live policy, replay recorded workloads through the proposed weights to check that utilisation improves and no agent is starved.

buildSteps.title: Learn the policy
buildSteps.detail: Introduce contextual bandits or reinforcement learning that choose assignments from observed outcomes, with strict rollback if a policy degrades service.

buildSteps.title: Operate and temper
buildSteps.detail: Watch for oscillation and feedback loops — a fast agent rewarded with more work can slow down, so the governor needs damping and fairness floors.

prerequisites.why: isolated, restartable execution units are the substrate the scheduler places work onto.
placing workloads across many machines at scale is a solved problem in general-purpose computing and provides the placement machinery.
efficiency can only be optimised if latency, cost and outcome are measured in a common format across heterogeneous agents.
running hundreds of agents concurrently multiplies serving cost, which caps how much the scheduler can usefully balance.
the governor needs a quality signal, not just a speed signal, or it will route work to fast but wrong agents.
learned allocation policies are researched in simulation but remain risky to run unguarded in production.

pathway.milestone: human-authored orchestration: workflow engines and RPA orchestrators dispatch work by fixed rules, with people setting priorities
pathway.unlocks: automation across tens to hundreds of bots inside a single organisation, with predictable behaviour and clear audit.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop scheduling within one operator, optimising measured latency, cost and quality rather than guessed priorities
pathway.unlocks: better utilisation of existing agents without changing them, plus automatic spillover when one agent or region is overloaded.

pathway.milestone: agent federation across teams or vendors, with shared task contracts and negotiated priorities instead of one central owner
pathway.unlocks: work can move to whichever provider is cheapest and fastest at that moment — market-style allocation, still largely theoretical.

pathway.milestone: a self-tuning layer that reallocates work across organisations under common governance, with evaluations and permissions strong enough to be trusted
pathway.unlocks: the closest realistic version of the 'hive' idea: many independent agents behaving as one coordinated fleet, bounded by hard safety and audit limits.
